newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Government sends two ships of food and fuel to northern Jaffna peninsula, amid Tamil separatist (LTTE) threats to attack vessels in northeastern waters. The LTTE torched a ship used to carry refugees and a North Korean merchant ship taking food, last month. The peninsula which was recaputred from rebels in 1996, is supplied by air and sea from Colombo.

Lamakers of the ruling People's Alliance (PA) coalition unanimously endorse draft constitution, which abolishes executive presidency and devolves part of the authority of the central government. The coalition members met at a two-day workshop in Kalutara, south of Colombo to thrash out differences and find a consensus.
PA lawmakers who met for two days to study draft constitution, called on President Kumaratunga to put the country on a war footing until the LTTE is defeated.
LTTE warns that any ship found in northereastern waters will be attacked.

Group of opposition United National Party members to meet Pakistan high commissioner in Colombo, to deliver a letter asking former prime minister Benazir Bhutto, not to participate in Anura Bandaranaike felicitation ceremonies, party sources said. Bhutto is due to attend a ceremony to mark Bandaranaike's two decades in politics.
